hero.title: Centurion University of Technology and Management, Odisha
hero.summary: Centurion’s Odisha agriculture and fisheries schools connect degree study with working fields, production enterprises and aquaculture facilities. At Paralakhemundi, agricultural learning includes rural and industrial attachments, while fisheries students study aquatic production, health, processing and resource management in a separate specialist school.

overview.heading: Two allied schools within one Odisha university
paragraphs: The M.S. Swaminathan School of Agriculture describes learning through fields, laboratories and enterprise activity. Its school page identifies agronomy, crop improvement, horticulture, soil science and extension as teaching and research areas. Student READY activities connect experiential work, rural exposure and agro-industrial attachment.

The School of Fisheries provides another applied pathway at Paralakhemundi. Its regulations describe aquaculture, fish processing, aquatic health and resource management, supported by training ponds, a hatchery and specialist production activity. Agriculture and fisheries therefore offer different practical settings within the university, and applicants can compare crop-based, engineering, agribusiness and aquatic-science routes according to their interests.

admissions.heading: Applying to CUTM
admissions.intro: Choose the agriculture, agricultural-engineering, fisheries or agribusiness route before checking entry rules. The fee table labels its Paralakhemundi rows 2026 but retains a 2025–26 heading; obtain a cohort-specific statement including other fees and accommodation.
eligibility_points: B.Sc. Agriculture: the programme page specifies 50% in 10+2 Science; obtain confirmation of its printed subject combination.
B.F.Sc.: the programme page states biology-containing science combinations and category-specific 50%/40% thresholds. These web criteria are undated by intake year.

scholarships.heading: Scholarships and financial support
scholarships.text: The published Amrit Kaal table includes Agricultural Engineering within its non-CSE B.Tech group at Paralakhemundi/Bhubaneswar. It sets first-year fee concessions by qualifying results. This is not evidence of the same award for B.Sc. Agriculture, M.Sc. Agriculture or Fisheries, and the page does not give a governing academic year.

schemes.name: Amrit Kaal scholarship: non-CSE B.Tech including Agri
schemes.details: The official table lists 10% for 60–70% qualifying marks and 15% for 70–80%; a separate top-score/JEE/OJEE band lists 20%. These are first-year fee concessions. Boundary wording, programme/campus eligibility and the current policy must be confirmed in the award letter.

placements.heading: Career support and outcomes
placements.text: The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

statistics.label: UG four-year programmes: 2024-2025
statistics.value: 253 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 170 placed; 83 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates ₹4,80,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2026, Agriculture and Allied Sectors, institutional submission

statistics.label: PG two-year programmes: 2024-2025
statistics.value: 54 graduates in minimum stipulated time; 37 placed; 13 selected for higher studies; median annual salary of placed graduates ₹4,30,000.
statistics.reporting_source: NIRF 2026, Agriculture and Allied Sectors, institutional submission

recognition.heading: Recognition and programme accreditation
recognition.text: Centurion is counted once in the audit. Its agriculture school has the 29 March 2024–28 March 2029 term; the School of Fisheries has the separate 8 February 2024–7 February 2029 term. Only the exact programmes below are supported by these records.

faqs.question: Why are two ICAR units shown for Centurion?
faqs.answer: Agriculture and fisheries have separate source rows; they belong to one Odisha university profile.

faqs.question: Does the fisheries degree use the agriculture accreditation dates?
faqs.answer: No. The fisheries record runs from 8 February 2024 to 7 February 2029.

faqs.question: Where is the fisheries school described in the regulations?
faqs.answer: The July 2022 regulations place it at the Paralakhemundi campus in Gajapati district.

faqs.question: Is agricultural engineering in the audit?
faqs.answer: Yes. B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering is included under the agriculture school record.

faqs.question: What distinguishes agriculture practical work?
faqs.answer: The school describes READY activities involving enterprise, rural and industrial exposure.

faqs.question: How are Centurion’s agriculture and fisheries fees quoted?
faqs.answer: The central table labels its Paralakhemundi rows 2026, while an older heading says 2025–26. Programme pages confirm annual B.Sc./B.F.Sc. charges and an MBA package; obtain a cohort-specific, itemised payable statement.

faqs.question: Are verified agriculture placement figures available?
faqs.answer: The NIRF 2026 agriculture/allied submission reports UG four-year programmes (2024-2025): 170 placed from 253 graduates in minimum time, with ₹4,80,000 median annual salary among those placed; PG two-year programmes (2024-2025): 37 placed from 54 graduates in minimum time, with ₹4,30,000 median annual salary among those placed. These are historical group-level outcomes, not specialisation-level placement promises.
